_note: Advice paraphrased from the cited extension sources (accessed 2026-10-14). It is general guidance; farmers should confirm with their local agricultural extension office.

management: Plant resistant varieties: the most efficient, reliable and cheapest control.
Apply balanced plant nutrients, especially nitrogen.
Ensure good drainage of flooded fields and nurseries.
Keep fields clean: remove weed hosts and plough under stubble, straw, ratoons and volunteer seedlings.
Allow fallow fields to dry to suppress the bacteria in soil and plant residues.
Bacterial leaf blight.source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank, Bacterial blight fact sheet: http://www.knowledgebank.irri.org/training/fact-sheets/pest-management/diseases/item/bacterial-blight

Brown spot.pathogen: Bipolaris oryzae (fungus; Texas Plant Disease Handbook)
management: Improve soil fertility: monitor soil nutrients and apply the fertilisers required.
On silicon-deficient soils, apply calcium silicate slag before planting.
Use resistant varieties (ask the local agriculture office for current lists).
Use fungicide seed treatments (e.g. iprodione, propiconazole, azoxystrobin, trifloxystrobin, carbendazim).
Treat seed with hot water (53-54 °C for 10-12 min) after an 8 h cold-water pre-soak.
Brown spot.source: IRRI Rice Knowledge Bank, Brown spot fact sheet: http://www.knowledgebank.irri.org/training/fact-sheets/pest-management/diseases/item/brown-spot

management: Leaf smut is a minor disease that appears late in the season and causes little or no economic loss.
No control measures are recommended for leaf smut.
No disease detected. Continue routine field monitoring.
